entities.name: Franciscus Accursius
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Franciscus Accursius (1225–1293) was an Italian lawyer, the son of the celebrated jurist and glossator Accursius. The two are often confused.

 Accursius was born into a prominent legal family in Bologna, Italy, around 1225. He studied law under his father and later became a renowned jurist in his own right.

 Accursius was a key figure in the development of legal glosses, which were explanatory notes added to medieval law codes. His most famous work, the 'Glossa Ordinaria,' became a standard reference for jurists and scholars across Europe.

 Accursius's work had a lasting impact on the development of law and legal education. He is remembered as one of the most important Italian jurists of the Middle Ages.

 Franciscus Accursius died in 1293, leaving behind a legacy that continues to shape the study of law and legal history.

 'The study of law is not an end in itself, but a means to understand the world and our place in it.' - Franciscus Accursius
